description: Timing parameter scaling configuration for different decision intervals
note: Current simulation: 1 timestep = 1 minute. Scaling changes what 1 timestep represents without changing timestep mechanics.

vehicle_speed.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (slower speed since less time per timestep)

service_time.description: Time for pickup/delivery operations in minutes
service_time.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (more timesteps needed for same real duration)

mean_interarrival_time.description: Average time between order arrivals in minutes
mean_interarrival_time.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (more frequent arrivals in timesteps)

mean_prep_time.description: Average food preparation time in minutes
mean_prep_time.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (more timesteps for same prep duration)

prep_time_var.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (scale variance with mean)

delivery_window.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (more timesteps for same deadline)

simulation_duration.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (more timesteps for same total duration)

cooldown_duration.description: Period with no new orders at end of simulation
cooldown_duration.scaling_rule: Divide by scaling_factor (more timesteps for same cooldown)

implementation_notes.approach: Keep timestep mechanics unchanged, just reinterpret what 1 timestep represents
implementation_notes.validation: Ensure all timing relationships remain proportionally correct
implementation_notes.testing: Test on small dataset first to verify behavior
considerations: Vehicle movement calculations may need verification
Order generation timing should maintain same real-world arrival patterns
Service time calculations should preserve realistic pickup/delivery durations
Deadline urgency should remain equivalent across scenarios
